raw_response:
I'm 47 years old, been working these fields since I was 17. Never spent a single day in school — can't read a word, but I know my land. My husband works at a factory in the county town, and my son is there too. They send money home, which helps buy fertilizer, but it means me and my daughter-in-law do most of the farm work ourselves. We have 36 mu: 18 mu in wheat that went in last October, then summer maize after harvest; 14 mu in cotton; and 4 mu of mungbean on the south plot for eating and selling.

The wheat is already in the ground. Last fall I put down compound fertilizer before planting — about one 50-jin bag for every two mu. Now it's March and the wheat is turning green. I always topdress with about half a bag of urea per mu at jointing. I don't skip this. Two years ago the spring turned dry and my neighbor Auntie Wang didn't topdress — her wheat barely made 200 jin per mu and she cried for a month. I irrigate three times: spring green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Water from the well costs 20 yuan each time, so I watch it, but you can't skip water in a dry spring.

Summer maize gets planted right after wheat harvest in mid-June. Sometimes you only have two or three days between harvest and planting — the window is tight. I buy hybrid seed fresh every year from the supply store, 60 yuan per mu. I hire Old Zhang's tractor to till and plant, 50 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the seed furrow at planting — about 50 jin per mu — then if the plants look yellow at jointing, I spread urea, about 30 jin per mu. If the summer rains are good I might skip the second fertilizer to save money. I irrigate twice if it's dry. Last year I got 470 jin per mu, hope it's the same.

Cotton is my biggest headache. I plant 14 mu in mid-to-late April with hybrid seed. It needs spraying for bollworms four or five times — the pesticide is expensive but you can't skip it. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow and topdress with urea at flowering. Last year I got greedy and put too much fertilizer — the cotton grew tall and leafy but didn't make bolls. I wasted money. This year I'm going back to what I know: about 60 jin compound at planting, 30 jin urea later. I irrigate three times. Picking is the killer. With 14 mu I have to hire women from the village, pay them by the kilo. That's my biggest cost, but 14 mu is too much for just me and my daughter-in-law.

Mungbean is easy. Saved seed from last year, plant in mid-May. A small handful of compound fertilizer in the furrow — about 20 jin per mu — water once, and let it grow. We eat mungbean soup all summer and sell the rest. About 100 jin per mu is fine.

I figure seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, water, and hired labor will cost about 16,500 yuan this year. That's a lot of money. My husband sent 8,000 yuan last month and I have 5,000 yuan saved from selling last year's maize. I'll borrow the rest from my brother if I have to. I'd rather spend a bit more and make sure I don't have a bad year. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps — I learned that in 2019 when the drought came. But I'm not being stupid either. Last year's cotton taught me that too much fertilizer is just wasting money.
